script: No one knows I stopped taking my life-saving medication a month ago.. After ten years of fighting my body every day, I decided that enough was enough. I didn't want a dramatic exit, like a quick exit, no messy. The UK doesn't do assisted death. Traveling abroad? Not possible for a disabled person, and I'd be a wreck. So I chose a slow exit, bestie. but here's the thing – I am still living it, but in a different way. My genetic illness means my immune system is busted. A tiny infection equals full‑blown sepsis, and I've seen that happen twice. I used to swallow high‑dose antibiotics every day, plus other meds, then I stopped a month ago. Nobody knows. then it hit me – I am basically on autopilot, waiting. Now I am sluggish, under the weather. I am still waiting quietly for something substantial to do the job. Honestly I am surprised it hasn't happened yet. No one else is watching; I am the only one in this. It will take hold before I end up in hospital. The audacity of living with this, knowing it will end naturally, is the only thing that feels right. Natural causes will be accepted, unlike suicide. I just wanted to admit it somewhere. I am still waiting for…
